rationale: The phenotypic spectrum of NFU1-related spastic paraplegia (SPG93 / complicated HSP) encompasses a milder, chronic allelic variant compared to the classic lethal infantile multiple mitochondrial dysfunctions syndrome 1 (MMDS1). In patients who survive into later childhood and adulthood (older patients), the phenotype expands from pure lower-limb spastic paraparesis to a complicated spastic-ataxia syndrome, frequently involving distal sensory-motor polyneuropathy, cerebellar ataxia, and white matter involvement with relapsing-remitting episodes and mild cognitive impairment.

evidence.text: Report of an NFU1-mutated patient presenting with a milder, slowly progressive spastic paraparesis phenotype with relapsing-remitting episodes, mild cognitive impairment, long survival, and mixed sensory-motor neuropathy emerging in the third decade.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence and age of onset of electrophysiologically verified distal axonal polyneuropathy across the entire Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) 19-patient SPG93 cohort?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether subclinical axonal neuropathy precedes overt sensory deficits in adolescents with NFU1 mutations would allow early electrodiagnostic discrimination from other forms of complicated HSP.

new_directions.question_text: Does elevated CSF or plasma glycine concentration reliably differentiate NFU1-related spastic paraplegia 93 from other recessive spastic ataxias such as SPAX5 or SPG7?
new_directions.rationale: NFU1 defects impair lipoic acid synthase and glycine cleavage system enzymes; validating biomarker discrimination would provide rapid confirmation prior to or alongside exome sequencing.
